Russian: Нет активных заданий. Проверьте зацепки или ответьте по радио.

Original English: No leads right now. The radio will crackle soon enough.
Russian: Пока нет зацепок. Скоро по радио появятся новые сообщения.

Original English: Daily ops post every morning at 6:00.
Russian: Ежедневные задания появляются каждое утро в 6:00.
ТРЕБУЕТСЯ НАПАРНИК — возьмите его с собой

Original English: Waiting on the radio - answer the call above.
Russian: Ожидается ответ по радио — примите вызов выше.

Original English: Someone else has taken point on this one.
Russian: Другой игрок уже взял на себя это задание.

Original English: No one rides with you yet. Help
Russian: Пока никто не сопровождает вас. Помогите

Original English: and they'll send someone. People you rescue may offer to come along too.
Russian: — и вам пришлют напарника. Спасённые люди тоже могут присоединиться.

Original English: Buddies follow you, fight beside you and remember what you do. Missions marked PARTNER REQUIRED need one along. Loyalty unlocks their personal story.
Russian: Напарники следуют за вами, сражаются рядом и помнят ваши поступки. Для заданий с пометкой «ТРЕБУЕТСЯ НАПАРНИК» нужен спутник. Доверие открывает личные истории.

Original English: How each group sees you. Standing changes how their people treat you on sight: Hostile and worse shoot first.
Russian: Как к вам относятся группировки. Репутация влияет на их поведение: враги могут открывать огонь без предупреждения.

They own the interstate and charge for it in blood.
Uniforms, radios, and orders from nobody they can name.
Thirty people behind barricaded pews, praying for a plan.
Badges and shotguns, enforcing a law that ended in July.

Keep an eye on the tree line.
We should fill the water jugs while it's quiet.
[sighs] My feet are shot. Don't tell anybody.
Russian: [вздыхает] Ноги отваливаются. Только никому не говори.

Original English: Check that car on the way past. Might be gas in it.
Russian: По пути проверь ту машину. Может, бензин остался.

Original English: I keep thinking I hear a generator. It's just the wind.
Russian: Мне всё кажется, будто слышу генератор. А это просто ветер.

Original English: Slow down. We don't have to run everywhere.
Lights off from here. They see it for miles.
Russian: Дальше без света. Его видно за километры.

Original English: Let's find somewhere with a door that locks.
Russian: Найдём место, где можно запереть дверь.

Original English: Rain'll cover the noise. Theirs too.
Russian: Дождь заглушит шум. И наш, и их.

Original English: [concerned] You're bleeding. Let me look at it.
Sit down a minute. That needs wrapping.
{buddy.first} doesn't say anything for a while.
Don't touch anything you don't need.
Whoever lived here didn't make it.
Russian: Те, кто здесь жил, не выжили.

Original English: Nobody's out at night unless they're up to something.
Russian: Ночью без причины никто не шатается.

Original English: Wet boots. That's how you lose toes.
Russian: Мокрые ботинки. Так и пальцев лишиться можно.

Original English: Can't hear a thing in this.
You're slowing down. Fix it before it gets worse.
Russian: Ты замедляешься. Займись этим, пока не стало хуже.

Original English: That needs cleaning. Now, not later.
Russian: Это надо обработать. Сейчас, не потом.

Original English: Another empty gas station. My favorite.
Remember when the worst thing was a flat tire.
Russian: Помнишь, когда худшей бедой было пробитое колесо?

Original English: I'd kill for a cup of coffee. Not literally. [laughs] Probably.
Russian: За чашку кофе я бы убил. Не буквально. [смеётся] Наверное.

Original English: You know what I miss? Ice.
Russian: Знаешь, чего мне не хватает? Льда.

Original English: Somebody's going to have to explain the bridge to me. Who blocks a bridge with a school bus.
If we find a working shower I'm moving in.
Russian: Если найдём работающий душ, я там поселюсь.

Original English: Great. The part of the day where everything's worse.
If I catch a cold after all this, I'm going to be furious.
Ugh. That's going to be in my hair.
Maybe stop getting hit. Just a thought.
[quietly] Lord, one more day. That's all I ask.
I said a prayer for the folks in that last house.
My mother would've had a casserole for every one of these people.
We'll get through this. I believe that.
I keep the Bible for the pages, mostly. Some nights I read it.
Somebody ought to bury them. Not today, though.
Say one for whoever's out there tonight.
Stay close. I don't like the dark anymore.
Well. It's good for the crops, if anybody's still growing any.
Hold still. Let me clean that.
You're not going anywhere till that's wrapped.
Russian: Пока не перевяжем, никуда не пойдёшь.

Original English: {buddy.first}: 'That wasn't right. You know it wasn't.'
Every one of these towns had a plan. Look how that went.
Somebody knew. Somebody always knows before the rest of us.
Don't tell me to calm down.
I'm not dying in some bathroom. I'm just not.
Let them come. I'm not sleeping anyway.
Of course. Of course it's raining.
Get up. Come on, get up.
{buddy.first} kicks a can across the road.
Drove a [[tow truck|school bus|delivery van]] in {town} before July. Doesn't talk about who [[they|she|he]] lost.
Was a [[nursing student|line cook|National Guard reservist|youth pastor|bartender]]. Still is, sort of.
Walked out of the Louisville evacuation alone. Nobody knows how.
Grew up on a farm outside {town}. Can field-dress a deer in four minutes.
Sold secrets to everyone, including you. Says that's over.
Used to carry out orders. Now carries yours. Hasn't decided if that's better.
{saga.settlement}'s best runner, before you showed up. {contact.first} says you two should stop competing and start covering each other.

Original English: Take it before someone else does.
Blocks are blocks, even when the dead walk them.
Brothers first. Everyone else pays the toll.
Everything is a deal. Even this.
the chain of command being a lie
Somebody has to keep the peace.
being the only ones left who care
running out of food before winter
You pull your weight, you eat.
This job needs a partner. Recruit or call a buddy first.
This one won't go away by ignoring it.
You step back. The story doesn't.
Here they come. Hold the line.

{saga.settlement} has a fence, a well and about a week of food. {warlord.last}'s crew has started stopping their people on the road and taking what they carry. Last night they took more than supplies.
A detachment of the {military.name} is still operating out of {checkpoint.name}. They have fuel, medicine and radios. They want something in return.
Now you know what the soldiers were sent here to do. Everyone wants your help, and you can't give it to all of them.
The cold is coming and there isn't enough of anything for everyone. It gets settled at {saga.stronghold}.
ran the feed store on Main
drove a school bus for twenty years
was a dispatcher at the sheriff's office
an Army medic in the Gulf
the school nurse at Muldraugh Elementary
ran a towing outfit on the bypass
did six years at Eddyville for armed robbery
was a guard at the county jail
{mole.name} had been passing information to {warlord.last}'s crew: patrol times, who was sick, where the supplies were kept.
{contact.name} traded {warlord.last} the location of the Guard's fuel cache to get {lost.first} back. Two soldiers died in the raid that followed.
The {military.name} have orders to take civilian fuel, vehicles and medicine for the pull-out, and to turn back anyone who tries to follow them out of the county.
There are only so many seats on the last trucks out. The {military.name}'s list has {doctor.name} on it. Nobody else from {saga.settlement} is.
{warlord.name} is {lost.first}'s {bloodWord}. {lost.first} got in that truck on {lost.his} own.
{warlord.last}'s crew is gone. {saga.settlement} goes into winter with its fence intact and enough to eat, if they're careful.
The {military.name} pulled out with what they came for. {saga.settlement} got a few crates of supplies and a promise nobody expects them to keep.
{warlord.last} runs the roads now, and you run them with {warlord.him}. People pay to pass. Most of them pay.
Nobody won. {saga.settlement} scattered, the soldiers are gone, and the roads around {saga.town} belong to the dead.

A ring of keys. One of them is newer than the rest.
Russian: Связка ключей. Один из них заметно новее остальных.

Original English: They take it. Then they smile.
Russian: Они забирают товар. А потом улыбаются.

Original English: They take it. A nod toward the building.
Russian: Они забирают товар и кивают в сторону здания.

Original English: [[Should've known.|Of course.|Never trust a smile out here.]]
Russian: [[Надо было догадаться.|Ну конечно.|Здесь нельзя доверять улыбкам.]]

Original English: Kill the target and their crew

[hesitant] This is a recorded... no. [clears throat] No, this is live. If anyone's on this channel, we're a group of survivors, about thirty of us. We have a fence, a well, and a little food. If you're alone out there, you don't have to be.
Russian: [нерешительно] Это запись... нет. [прочищает горло] Нет, я говорю вживую. Если кто-то слушает эту частоту: нас около тридцати выживших. Есть забор, колодец и немного еды. Если вы там одни, вам необязательно оставаться в одиночестве.

Original English: I hear you. Who is this?
What do you want in return?
How long have you been broadcasting?
Russian: Как давно вы выходите в эфир?

Original English: I'm the one who ended up in charge, mostly because nobody else wanted it. We've got farmers, a mechanic, a couple of teachers. What we don't have is anyone who can go out on the roads and come back.
Russian: Так вышло, что я здесь главный. Наверное, потому что больше никто не захотел. У нас есть фермеры, механик, пара учителей. Не хватает только человека, который сможет ездить по дорогам и возвращаться живым.

Original English: I'm the one who ended up in charge, I guess. Somebody had to make the lists and keep people fed. We've got good people here. We just don't have anyone who can go out on the roads and come back.
Russian: Похоже, я здесь за главного. Кто-то ведь должен составлять списки и кормить людей. У нас хорошие люди, но никто не может безопасно ездить по окрестным дорогам.

Original English: Fair question. A bed, a share of the food, somebody awake while you sleep. That's what we've got. In return we need help getting supplies. Medicine, mostly.
Russian: Справедливый вопрос. Кровать, доля еды и тот, кто не спит, пока вы отдыхаете. Это мы можем предложить. А нам нужна помощь с припасами, прежде всего с лекарствами.

Original English: Every hour, for about a week. We run the radio off a car battery. You're the first person who's answered who didn't want something.
Russian: Каждый час уже около недели. Рацию питаем от автомобильного аккумулятора. Вы первый, кто ответил и ничего не потребовал.

Original English: Every hour for a week, on a car battery. The last two people who answered wanted to know how many guns we had. So you'll understand if I'm careful.
Russian: Каждый час на протяжении недели, от автомобильного аккумулятора. Последние двое спросили, сколько у нас оружия. Так что поймите мою осторожность.

Original English: There's also a crew working the roads around here. They stop our people when they go out, take whatever they're carrying. Nobody's been killed yet. I'd like to keep it that way.
Russian: По здешним дорогам ещё ездит одна банда. Они останавливают наших людей и отбирают всё, что те несут. Пока никого не убили. Хотелось бы, чтобы так и осталось.

Original English: Where are you? I'll come to you.

Local people, mostly. Some of them I knew before. They're hungry like everybody else, they've just decided it's easier to take it from us than find it. They're not stupid, and there's more of them every week.
Russian: В основном местные. Кого-то я знал раньше. Они голодны, как и все, но решили, что отбирать у нас проще, чем искать самим. Они не глупы, а людей у них с каждой неделей всё больше.

Original English: Where are you? I'll come to you.
Come in slow, from the road side, with your hands where we can see them. People here are jumpy. I'll tell them you're coming.
Russian: Подъезжайте медленно со стороны дороги. Руки держите на виду. Наши люди сейчас нервничают. Я предупрежу их о вас.

Original English: All right. We're on this channel every hour if you change your mind. Stay safe out there.
Russian: Ладно. Если передумаете, мы на этой частоте каждый час. Берегите себя.

Original English: {contact.name} has been on the emergency channel for a week. The group is holding out at {saga.settlement}. Go and see them.
Russian: {contact.name} уже неделю выходит на связь по аварийной частоте. Группа держит оборону в {saga.settlement}. Нужно добраться до них.

Original English: [[Smoke from a chimney. Washing on a line.|You hear a generator before you see the fence.|Someone has painted HELP on the roof. Someone else painted over it.]]
Clear the infected along the fence
A stranger came in to {saga.settlement} and stayed.
[relieved] You came. Good. Sorry about the rifle at the gate. In the summer we let a man in who said he was a trader. Two people didn't wake up.
Russian: [с облегчением] Вы пришли. Хорошо. Извините за винтовку у ворот. Летом мы впустили человека, который назвался торговцем. Утром двое наших уже не проснулись.

Original English: [relieved] You came. Thank God. Sorry about the rifle at the gate. We let a man in over the summer who said he was a trader. We lost two people that night. We're more careful now.
Russian: [с облегчением] Вы пришли, слава богу. Извините за винтовку у ворот. Летом мы впустили торговца и в ту ночь потеряли двоих. Теперь мы осторожнее.

Original English: How many people do you have here?
How many of them can fight?

Russian: Что вам нужно в первую очередь?

Original English: Thirty-one this morning. Six kids. A few old folks who can't walk far. My {lost.kin} is here too. Most of us were neighbors before. Now we're all we've got.
Russian: Сегодня утром был тридцать один человек. Шестеро детей. Несколько стариков, которые далеко не уйдут. Мой {lost.kin} тоже здесь. Раньше мы были соседями, теперь друг у друга только мы и остались.

Original English: Maybe five who can shoot straight. Eleven rifles if you count the ones nobody has ammunition for. That's why they keep stopping us on the road. They know.
Russian: Может, пятеро умеют нормально стрелять. Одиннадцать винтовок, если считать те, на которые нет патронов. Вот почему они останавливают нас на дорогах. Они всё знают.

Original English: The fence. The dead pile up on the north side every night and we're using bullets we can't spare to keep it standing. Clear it out, then go and see our medic. There's a list.
Russian: Забор. Мертвецы каждую ночь скапливаются у северной стороны. Мы тратим патроны, которых и так мало, лишь бы он устоял. Зачистите подходы, а потом идите к медику. У него есть список.

Original English: After that we talk about the road crew. Let's see how today goes first.
Russian: Потом поговорим о банде на дороге. Сначала посмотрим, как пройдёт сегодняшний день.

Original English: You're the new one. Sit down, let me look at that hand. I'm out of antibiotics, I've got two people with infected cuts and a kid with an ear infection that won't clear. Everything I need is on this list.
Russian: Так вы у нас новенький. Присядьте, дайте взглянуть на руку. Антибиотики кончились, у двоих воспалились раны, а у ребёнка никак не проходит ушная инфекция. Всё необходимое записано в этом списке.

Original English: You're the new one. Sit. Let me see the hand. I was a nurse, not a doctor, so don't expect miracles. No antibiotics, no sutures, two infected cuts I can't do anything about. Here's the list.
Russian: Так вы новенький. Садитесь, покажите руку. Я была медсестрой, а не врачом, чудес не ждите. Ни антибиотиков, ни шовного материала, две воспалённые раны, и я ничего не могу сделать. Вот список.

Original English: [nervous] You're the new one. Sorry, I haven't slept. Let me look at you. Do you go out on the east road much? No reason. People just talk about who goes where.
Russian: [нервно] Вы новенький. Простите, я не спал. Дайте взглянуть на вас. Вы часто ездите по восточной дороге? Просто спрашиваю. Люди обсуждают, кто куда ездит.

Original English: Why do you want to know?
Just tell me what you need.
Because I'm the one who stitches up whoever comes back hurt. That's all. Here. The list.
Russian: Потому что именно мне приходится зашивать раны тем, кто возвращается. Только поэтому. Вот. Список.

Original English: Antibiotics. Sutures. Disinfectant. Anything from a pharmacy. People are dying of things that would've been a ten-minute visit to the clinic a few months ago.
Russian: Антибиотики. Шовный материал. Дезинфицирующие средства. Всё, что найдёте в аптеке. Люди умирают от того, что ещё пару месяцев назад лечилось за десять минут.

Original English: I'll see what I can find.
[First Aid] Let me help with the patients first.
You actually know what you're doing. Okay. That's one less fever tonight. Thank you.
Russian: Вы и правда знаете, что делаете. Хорошо, хотя бы у одного человека сегодня спадёт температура. Спасибо.

Original English: Find the medicine on the list

Russian: {doctor.name} нужны антибиотики и шовный материал. Возможно, в {site.name} ещё остались медикаменты.

Original English: might not have been picked clean yet.
[relieved] The boy with the infected leg is going to keep it. I wasn't sure he would. Come see me when you get hurt. You will.
Russian: [с облегчением] Парень с воспалённой ногой её сохранит. Я уже сомневался. Если получите ранение, приходите ко мне. А вы его получите.

Original English: [hesitant] You brought all of it. I didn't think anyone would. [lowers voice] Listen... be careful who you trust here. Even people who've been good to you. Forget it. Thank you.
Russian: [нерешительно] Вы принесли всё. Я не думал, что у кого-то получится. [тише] Слушайте... будьте осторожны, выбирая, кому доверять. Даже здесь. Забудьте. Спасибо.

Original English: [[Engines behind you. Somebody saw you.|A shout from the roof, then people moving.|A truck pulls out of the lot and turns your way.]]
. Find out how many there are and how they operate.
Someone from {saga.settlement} scouted the road crew at their base.
There's more of them than you think, and they're better armed.
Russian: Их больше, чем вы думаете, и они лучше вооружены.

Original English: They keep a book. Names, what people carry, when they travel.
Russian: Они ведут записи: имена, грузы, время поездок.

Original English: Thank you for not dressing it up. Everyone else here tells me what they think I want to hear.
Russian: Спасибо, что сказали как есть. Остальные обычно говорят лишь то, что я хочу услышать.

Original English: [sharply] Don't. I saw your face when you came in. Just tell me straight.
Russian: [резко] Не надо. Я видел ваше лицо, когда вы вошли. Скажите прямо.

Original English: So they're organized. That's worse than hungry. Hungry people make mistakes.
Russian: Значит, они организованы. Это хуже простого голода. Голодные люди ошибаются.

Original English: The one who runs things for them out there used to fix tractors. Nice enough, before. Now he's the one who stops our people on the road. If they come here, he'll be leading them.
Russian: Тот, кто сейчас командует у них, раньше ремонтировал тракторы. Неплохой был человек. А теперь останавливает наших людей. Если банда придёт сюда, он будет впереди.

Original English: Someone keeps breaking in on the settlement's channel reading lists of numbers. {contact.first} traced the strongest signal to
A logbook of frequencies and times. The callsign on the cover is {informant.alias}.
Use the frequency in the logbook
[amused] So you're the one who broke into my place. It's fine. I don't keep anything there worth shooting someone over.
Russian: [весело] Так это вы забрались ко мне в дом. Ничего страшного. Там нет ничего, за что стоило бы стрелять.

Original English: Who is this? How did you get this frequency? Were you in my house? Please tell me you didn't touch the antenna.
Why are you breaking in on our channel?
Russian: Зачем вы влезаете в наш эфир?

Original English: I listen. Everybody's on the radio now. The road crew, the Guard, your people. I write down what I hear and trade it for food. It's honest work, more or less.
Russian: Я слушаю. Теперь все сидят на радио: бандиты, гвардия, ваши люди. Записываю, что слышу, и меняю сведения на еду. Почти честная работа.

Original English: Because your people are going to need what I hear, and I'm going to need things your people have. Let's meet in person. Come alone. Don't come in shooting.
Russian: Потому что вашим людям ещё пригодится то, что я слышу. А мне понадобится кое-что от вас. Встретимся лично. Приходите одни и без стрельбы.

Original English: You came. Most people don't, they just get angry on the radio. Sit down.
Russian: Вы всё-таки пришли. Большинство только злятся по радио. Садитесь.

Original English: You came alone? Okay. Okay. Sorry, I don't do this much. Sit. Please. I'll keep my hands on the table.
What do you know about the road crew?
Russian: Что вы знаете о дорожной банде?

Original English: [Intimidate] You're going to tell me everything you know.
Russian: [Запугивание] Вы расскажете мне всё, что знаете.

Original English: They keep a list of every group around here. How many people, what they have, how many can fight. Your people are near the top, ever since they started broadcasting.
Russian: Они ведут список каждой группы в округе. Численность, запасы, оружие. Ваши люди почти наверху списка с тех пор, как начали вещать по радио.

Original English: All right, all right. They move people through their place every few days. People who can't pay. Some of them don't come back out. That's all I know, I swear.
Russian: Ладно, ладно. Они раз в несколько дней привозят людей к себе на базу. Тех, кто не может заплатить. Некоторые обратно не выходят. Клянусь, больше я ничего не знаю.

Original English: [laughs] I've been threatened by people with bigger guns than you. Do you want to try that again, nicely?
Russian: [смеётся] Мне угрожали люди с оружием посерьёзнее вашего. Может, попробуете ещё раз, только вежливо?

Original English: Batteries. Radio parts. And somewhere to sleep behind a fence when it gets bad. I'll keep listening. When I hear something you need, I'll call.
Russian: Батарейки. Детали для рации. И место за забором, где можно переночевать, когда станет совсем плохо. Я продолжу слушать и позвоню, если услышу что-то важное.

Original English: Word is the road crew is coming to {saga.settlement}, probably at night. The fence needs repairs and every rifle on it.
Get some rest while you can.
Headlights on the road. Three vehicles.
The road crew hit {saga.settlement} at night and was driven off.
The road crew got through {saga.settlement}'s fence. People died.
[exhales] We didn't lose anyone. [softly] First time since the summer that I haven't had to write a name down in the morning.
They'll be back. With more people.
I know. But now they know it costs them something to come here. That might be enough to make them pick somebody else.
They held because you were on the fence with them. Don't let it go to your head.
[[That's the one from the fence!|Get down!|Over there!]]
{lieutenant.name} - '{lieutenant.moniker}' - led the attack on the fence. {contact.first} won't say it out loud, but people at {saga.settlement} want him dealt with.
[panicked] Okay! Okay, I'm done. I'm unarmed. Look, I've got information. I can be useful to you. Just let me talk.
[laughs] Look at that. You actually did it. You know what, I'm almost glad. I was getting bored. Go on, then. Or don't. I know things you want to know.
[Intimidate] Tell me everything, or this goes badly for you.
At their base, same as everybody. But there's a loading dock around back. Nobody watches it after midnight. That has to be worth something.
The loading dock, around back, nobody on it after midnight. They keep people they've taken in the walk-in cooler. And somebody at your place is talking to them. I don't know who. I swear I don't.
You're not going to do anything. I can tell.
That's it? That's your scary voice? I've done worse to people for less.
Go. If I see you again, you're dead.
Go back to your boss. Tell them to leave the settlement alone.
Yeah. Okay. You won't see me. Nobody will.
Huh. Mercy. Okay. You'll regret that, but okay.
{lieutenant.name} was let go and left the area.
I'll tell them. They won't listen. They'll come at you harder, and I'll be with them.
[[Two trucks out front. Fresh tire marks.|Music coming from inside.|A pair of shoes on the steps.]]
[[Who the hell are you?|Get to the doors!|Somebody followed us!]]
[[Help me!|In the back!|They locked the door!]]
The road crew stopped the water run at dawn and took {lost.name}, {contact.first}'s {lost.kin}. {doctor.first} followed the tire tracks to
The attempt to get {lost.first} back from
[panicked] Are you there? Please pick up. They stopped the water run at dawn. Three trucks. They took my {lost.kin}. Just put {lost.him} in the back of a truck and drove off.
[urgent] Pick up. Now, please. They hit the water run this morning. They took my {lost.kin}. Threw {lost.him} in a truck and drove off. Nobody else was hurt. They only wanted {lost.him}.
Our medic followed the tracks most of the way. We know where they went. It's their ground out there. People who go there to argue don't come back.
Guards on the doors, maybe four or five. They keep people away from the windows, in the back. The guard on the back door carries the keys. Or you go in loud and hope you're faster than the dead.
I need time to get ready.
Because {lost.he}'s young and healthy and can work. Because it'll make the rest of us do what they say. I don't know. Does it matter?
[voice breaking] It doesn't matter why. I'm sorry. I'm not... please. Just get {lost.him} out of there.
[bitterly] Then I'll go myself. I'll probably die in the parking lot, and {lost.he}'ll still be in there.
[shaky] You're not one of them. Did my... did they send you? Okay. There were others in here. Two days ago. They moved them somewhere else.
About time. No, sorry. Sorry. Thank you. There were other people in here too. They moved them two days ago. I heard them talking about it.
We'll worry about them later. Let's get you out.
Stay behind me. Run when I tell you.
There's a door by the loading dock. I'll go for the road. Just keep them off me.
[urgently] Wait. Stop. You don't understand. The one in charge here, that's my real parent. Nobody at the settlement knows. I wasn't dragged anywhere. I got in the truck.
[Persuade] Your family back home is falling apart. Come back. You can be angry at all of us later.
It's your choice. I won't drag you anywhere.
They have people locked in the back. Is that who you want to be with?
Fine. I'll come back. But I'm not done here.
No. Let go of me. I'm staying.
Nobody's ever said that to me. Okay. I'll come back. For now. Because you asked.
[quietly] I heard them crying at night. I kept telling myself it wasn't what it sounded like. Okay. Get me out of here.
[softly] {lost.He}'s asleep. First real sleep in three days. I keep going in to check {lost.he}'s still breathing. We don't have much, but what we have, you're welcome to.
There were other people in there. They were moved.
They're not going to let this go.
So they're holding people. Not just taking supplies. Then sooner or later somebody's going to have to go there. I was hoping it wouldn't come to that.
No, they won't. And there's something else. Somebody's been talking on the old Guard channel. Military talk. Somebody new is in the area.
So now you know. It was a long time ago, and it ended badly. I didn't tell you because I was afraid you wouldn't go.
I did. I'd do it again. That's what being a parent is now.
Yeah. I think you would have.
[stunned] What do you mean, stayed? {lost.He} chose to stay there? Get out. No. Sorry. Sit down. I don't have anybody else to say this to.
Maybe it was {lost.first}'s choice to make.
{officer.full} of the {military.name} has been calling on the old Guard channel. They're holding
[[Sandbags, wire, a hand-painted sign: STOP 50 METERS.|Someone is watching you through a scope the whole way in.|A Humvee with no tires, used as a barricade.]]
Unknown station, this is a Kentucky National Guard detachment. We've been monitoring your traffic. We'd like to speak with whoever's been running supplies for the group by the river. Over.
Whoever's been running supplies out of that settlement, this is the Guard. What's left of it out here, anyway. We've been listening to you for a while. We should talk.
I don't work for the government.
A detachment of about twenty. We hold a position nearby with fuel, medical supplies and a working generator. We need people who know the area. Over.
Neither does anybody else these days. This isn't a draft. It's a trade. Over.
Come to the checkpoint in daylight, weapon slung. We'll talk face to face. Out.
Sit down. There's coffee if you want it. It's the real stuff, the last of it. Consider it a gesture of good faith.
Sit. Coffee's real, last can we have. I'm not going to make a speech. I'm tired and you look tired, so let's just talk.
What do you want from me?
[Military] Where's the rest of your unit?
A command post outside the exclusion zone. They call twice a week. They ask how many civilians we've processed. I don't like that word either.
Dead, or gone home. Most of them left in July and didn't come back. I've got under twenty people and orders I'm not allowed to share. You asked that like someone who's served.
Where they need to be. Next question.
There's a building I need cleared so we can use it as an aid station. The road crew is living in it. Help my people clear it, and your settlement gets put on our supply list. Medicine, ammunition.
And what does that cost the settlement?
A list of names. Who's there, who's sick, who has a trade. It's standard procedure. Nothing they need to worry about.
A list of names. Who's sick, who's healthy, who has a trade. They tell me it's standard. [sighs] I stopped asking what they do with the lists.
That sounds like more than paperwork.
for an aid station. The road crew is using it. A fireteam will meet you on the approach.
Meet the fireteam on the approach
[[The sergeant nods at you. 'We go when you go.'|'Stay out of our line of fire and we'll get along fine.']]
Relay's up. Good work. Your settlement goes on the supply list, like I said. Over.
Soon. One more thing. Somebody on the civilian bands has been talking to you. A ham operator. We hear everything out here. Be careful what you buy from people who sell to everyone. Out.
On paper it's a collection point. For civilians who need evacuation. Don't read too much into it. Out.
A helicopter supply drop for the {military.name} came down off target near
Two people are on the radio
You have our crate. Bring it to the checkpoint. That isn't a request.
I'm on this channel too. There's antibiotics in that crate. We have three people who won't make it through the week without them. I'm not ordering you. I'm asking.
The supply drop went to the soldiers.
The supply drop went to {saga.settlement}. The soldiers noticed.
[Persuade] Split it. Medicine to the settlement, ammunition to the checkpoint.
Fine. Fine. Bring me the ammunition. Out.
I said it wasn't a request. We'll remember this. Out.
The {military.name} will protect {saga.settlement} if they hand over their guns and accept a curfew. {contact.first} and {doctor.first} disagree, loudly. Everyone wants to hear what you think.

[angry] Hand over our guns to people who talk about processing civilians. We've kept everyone here alive since summer with eleven rifles. I'm not giving them up because somebody in a uniform asked nicely.
I want to say yes. I want someone else to be responsible for once. But I've heard how they talk on that radio. If we give up the guns, we can't ever take them back.
You can't hold off the road crew alone forever.
We're not alone. We've got you now. Don't we?
Then say so at the meeting. People listen to you now.
They have antibiotics. Insulin. A working autoclave. I've watched people die here from things I could have treated in a clinic in an afternoon. I don't care about the guns. I care about the patients.
[exhausted] I buried four people this month. Four. They have insulin and antibiotics. I don't care whose flag is on the gate anymore. I'm tired of digging.
And when they want more than guns?
Then we deal with it, alive. That's the whole point.
Thank you. Pride isn't a plan. It's just a slower way to die.
Everybody's here. Go ahead. Say what you came to say.
Take the deal. Hand in the guns.
[Persuade] Take the medicine. Keep the guns. Make them earn the rest.
[resigned] Then that's the vote. Somebody box up the rifles. I'll hand mine over myself.
Then I hope you're as good as they say. Because we're on our own now.
That's the first idea tonight nobody's yelling about. All right. We do it that way.
{saga.settlement} worked out a deal with the soldiers.
Half of them want the guns gone and half want them loaded. Great. Now we're two groups.
The meeting at {saga.settlement} ended in a shouting match.
{warlord.last}'s crew has blocked the only clear road to the river and is charging people to pass. Trade runs have stopped. Pay, talk your way through, or clear it.
Push the cars out of the road
The roadblock on the river road was cleared.
Road's open. It just costs something to use it now. Pay and you can go back and forth all week. Don't pay and you can go around. It's about thirty miles.
[Lie] My people already paid this week. Check with your boss.
Nobody keeps track of anything around here anyway. Go on. Don't tell anybody.
Yeah, okay. This isn't worth getting shot over.
Nice try. [shouting] Hey! Get over here!
{lost.first} wants to go back to the house {lost.he} lived in before the evacuation. {contact.first} won't let {lost.him} go alone.
An evacuation intake form from July, and a second page: a list headed ESSENTIAL PERSONNEL. Nurses, mechanics, an electrician. Everyone else is just a number.
You found them. I just wanted to remember what everybody looked like before. Before they looked scared all the time.
You actually found them. I figured they'd burned or something. I just wanted proof we were normal once.
There was paperwork from the evacuation too. A list.
At the evac center they split everyone into two lines. People with useful jobs went on buses. Everyone else waited. We waited three days. Then the fence went down and we ran.
Nurses. Doctors. Mechanics. Anyone who could keep the soldiers going. They didn't even pretend it was about saving people.
Keep that to yourself for now.
Yeah. Thanks for coming with me. You didn't have to.
{informant.name} says it's urgent, and that it can't go over the air. Meet at
[[There! By the door!|Don't let them leave!|Go, go!]]
Not on the radio. Not this one. Same place as before, after dark. Come by yourself. It's about your settlement, and people are listening.
I can't say it on the air. I can't. Meet me tonight, after dark. Please come alone. I think they're listening to everything now.
[quietly] You came. I knew you would. That's what they were counting on.
[crying] You came. Oh God, you actually came. I'm so sorry. I'm so sorry.
[voice breaking] They have my brother. Since August. Every time I told you something, I told them first. Supply runs, patrol times, where you sleep. I'm sorry. They're already outside.
Shut the door. Look at these. Letters. I took them off one of their runners. Look at the handwriting.
Patrol times. Who's sick and who's armed. When the supply runs go out. Your medic's been writing to them for weeks. And I think the runner I took these from was followed.
You ever wonder why they let the kid go so easy? Or how they knew where the Guard kept their fuel?
Your leader traded them the location of the Guard's fuel cache to get the kid back. The raid on that cache killed two soldiers. And I'm pretty sure I was followed here.
Someone you trusted sold out {saga.settlement}. Everyone is waiting to see what you do about it.
I'm not going to beg. Do what you have to. But if you ever get inside their place, my brother's in the cooler in the back. He didn't do anything.
[crying] Please. I know. I know what I did. I'm not asking for me. My brother's in there, in the cooler. If you ever go in, please get him out.
Leave. If I see you again, I won't stop to talk.
[Intimidate] You work for me now. You tell them what I want them to hear.
Come with me. We'll get your brother out together.
Thank you. I'll get him out myself. Or I'll die trying.
{informant.name} was run out of the county.
Fine. I'll feed them whatever you want. I'm dead either way. At least this way I'm useful.
No. I'm done taking orders from anyone.
You're serious. After all that. Okay. I know the back roads and I know every frequency they use. I'm with you.
{me.first} took in {informant.name}. Not everyone at {saga.settlement} agreed.
[defensive] You found the letters. I can see it. Before you say anything: they have insulin. I have two diabetics here. Every letter bought a month of insulin. Every one.
You found the letters. I know how it looks. They have insulin. I have two diabetics. I told myself I was saving lives. I'm not sure anymore.
People died because of what you told them.
[First Aid] There were other ways to get insulin.
And people lived. I did the math. Every night, I did the math.
Were there? Where? You weren't here in July. You don't know what it was like.
Everyone's watching. It's your call. They'll go along with whatever you decide.
We need a medic more than we need a hanging. They stay.
Who's going to set the next broken leg? You? Fine.
I won't write to them again. I swear it.
{doctor.name} informed on {saga.settlement} and was allowed to stay.
[shaky] Then who takes care of them now?
You know. I can see it on your face. Go on, say it.
You traded the soldiers' lives for {lost.first}.
[firmly] I traded strangers' lives for my {lost.kin}. Yes. I'd do it again. Anyone would. Most people just never have to choose.
Because you'd have looked at me the way you're looking at me now.
Tell everyone the truth. Let them decide.
This stays between us. You owe me.
Turn yourself in to the soldiers.
Yeah. I figured you'd say that. That's why people trust you.
{contact.name} told {saga.settlement} the truth and stepped down. {doctor.name} is in charge now.
Then I owe you. For as long as either of us is alive.
[bitterly] You'd hand me over to them. Okay. Then my {lost.kin} has nobody.
The Guard's radios are encrypted, but the old phone line out of
still runs past a junction box down the road. Splice in and listen.

Confirm the pull-out is on schedule. You are authorized to requisition fuel, vehicles and medical supplies from civilian holdouts in your sector. Civilians are not to be moved past the cordon. Repeat, not past the cordon.
[hesitant] Sir, if we take their fuel and their medicine, half of them won't make it through the winter.
Sir, understood. For the record, taking their fuel and medicine will cost lives over the winter.
Noted. Your orders stand. The cordon stays closed. Acknowledge.
Confirm your seat count for the last convoy. Priority is your personnel, then medical and technical civilians on the list we sent. No one else boards. We don't have the room.
Sir, the medic at the settlement is on that list. Nobody else from there is. They're going to find out.
Understood, sir. The settlement's medic is on the list. I'll make the approach.
Then make sure the medic is on the truck before they do. Acknowledge.
Everyone knows now. Everyone is calling you.
You heard it. We all did. I don't know how to fight soldiers. I don't even know if we can. But we're not giving them what we need to get through the winter. Not without a fight.
This is the Guard. I know what you heard. I didn't write those orders, but they're happening with or without me. Work with me and I can keep it orderly. Nobody has to get hurt.
It's me. I know what you heard. I'm not going to defend it. It's happening either way. If you're with me, I can at least make sure nobody gets shot over a fuel tank.

Hey. It's me. You've been a real problem for me this season, so I'll keep it short. The soldiers are leaving and they're taking everything with them. When they're gone, somebody has to run things around here. Come talk to me.

[amused] There you are. You know, I've thought about killing you a lot this season. Funny thing is, I like you. The soldiers are running, your farmers are going to starve, and I'm the only one with a plan. Come see me.
Three channels. Static in between. Your thumb on the key.
[{military.name}] I'll work with you. Keep it orderly.
{me.first} sided with the {military.name}. {saga.settlement} stopped answering the radio.
The {military.name} can't coordinate the requisition without their radio. Take it out and buy {saga.settlement} some time.
Eleven rifles won't stop a Guard detachment.
might still have a locked cabinet nobody's opened.
{doctor.first} wants the sick, the old and the kids moved to
before the soldiers come. Someone has to secure it and hold it until they're settled.
Hold the building while the others arrive
The children and the sick were moved out of {saga.settlement}.
The soldiers are coming for the fuel and the medicine. Trucks on the county road tonight. {saga.settlement} isn't handing anything over.
Headlights. A loudspeaker: 'This is a lawful requisition. Step away from the fence.'
The {military.name} pulled back from {saga.settlement} without the fuel.
The soldiers took everything from {saga.settlement}. People started leaving the next day.
[relieved] It's morning and we're still here. With our fuel. I keep saying it out loud to make sure it's true.
Your people did this. Not me.
Maybe. Or maybe they'll just leave like they were always going to. Either way, the road crew is still out there, and they watched all of this.
Both of us did. Now we have to finish it. The road crew is still out there, and they're not going to wait for spring.
to go over the plan in person.
I wanted you to hear it from me and not from a wiretap. I don't like these orders. I'm going to carry them out anyway, because the alternative is someone who does like them.
Thanks for coming in. Here's the situation. The orders are clear and they're lawful. I'd rather carry them out with someone who knows the area than without.
Then let's do it with as little harm as possible.
That's the idea. First, the road crew is sitting on the route we need for the convoy. Clear them out. Then we deal with the rest.
Don't say it like it's easy. It isn't. It shouldn't be.
Good. Then we're on the same page. First job is the road crew on our convoy route.
If there's another way, find it before Command finds out I'm looking for one. That's all I can give you.
There isn't. I've looked. Clear the road.
Meet the soldiers at the staging point
and the road past it. The convoy needs that road.
The convoy needs fuel and medical supplies. {saga.settlement} has both. You know where they keep them.
Take the fuel cans from the shed
Take the medicine from the clinic
[angry] I watched you do it. You walked right past the room where the kids sleep and took the fuel that keeps them warm. Say something. Anything.
I left some of it behind the shed. Enough for a few weeks.
They'd have taken it by force. This way nobody got shot.
Behind the shed. Okay. That's something. It's not enough, but it's something. Now get out.
Someone left fuel hidden behind {saga.settlement}'s shed.
[bitterly] Nobody got shot. Right. We'll just freeze instead. Thank you so much.
{saga.settlement} lost its fuel and medicine to the {military.name}.
{doctor.name} is on the evacuation list. {officer.full} wants them at {checkpoint.name} before the settlement finds out nobody else is.
[[Somebody from the settlement is following you.|You hear shouting behind you.|Two people from the settlement on the road behind you, armed.]]
I know why you're here. They told me I'm on a list. A seat on a truck out of the county. Just me. Not the kids, not anyone else.
I know. They told me. A seat on a truck, just for me. And the worst part is part of me wants to go. I'm so tired.
[Persuade] Out there you can help a lot more people. Go.
You're coming either way. I'm sorry.
Don't go. Hide. I'll tell them you ran.
Maybe. Maybe that's true. Let me write down the doses for the people here first. Then I'll go.
No. These people need me more than some base camp does. You'll have to make me.
[coldly] Then let's go. And you can explain it to them when they get sick.
Thank you. I won't forget this. I don't think the soldiers will either.
{doctor.name} disappeared before the {military.name} could take them.
{warlord.name}'s crew knows the soldiers are pulling out, and they want the convoy. They're coming for {checkpoint.name}.
Command wants a full report. Everything we did and why. I'm the one writing it. How do you want it to read?
Write that the road crew took the supplies.
All right. I'll sign it. If they want someone to blame, it'll be me. Now let's finish the road crew before the convoy rolls.
Smoothly. Sure. Let's deal with the road crew before I have time to think about it.
That's convenient. I hate that it's convenient. Fine. Let's go make it true.
{warlord.name} is waiting at {saga.stronghold}. Walk in the front. Nobody's supposed to shoot.
[[Nobody raises a gun. They just watch you.|Somebody laughs. Somebody else tells them to shut up.|A kid with a rifle that's too big for him opens the gate.]]
Sit down. You want something to drink? We've got coffee, and whiskey if you'd rather. I'll be straight with you. I've got forty people here who eat every day. I'd like it to stay that way.
[cheerfully] Sit, sit. Don't look at the guys by the door, they're just there for decoration. Mostly. You know, I almost had you killed twice this season. I'm glad I didn't. You're more fun alive.
What do you want from me?

Because people can work. Food runs out. Fuel runs out. A person who can dig a ditch or fix an engine keeps being useful. The soldiers are leaving people to freeze. I put them to work and feed them. You tell me which is worse.
[laughs] Because I can. That's the honest answer. Nobody's coming to stop me. You'd do the same if you thought about it long enough. Everyone would.
I know where {lost.he} is. I know {lost.he} came back with you. If you ever get the chance, tell {lost.him} the door's still open here. That's all.
Two things. The settlement has medicine I need. The soldiers have a supply truck I need more. Bring me both, and you're one of us. Food, a bed, people who'll back you up.
I'm not working for you. I'm working with you.
Then you walk out the same way you came in, and next time we meet it won't be over coffee. Your call.
Then you walk out. And I'll find out where you sleep. I always do. Your call.
{saga.settlement}'s medicine is in {doctor.first}'s clinic. They still open the gate for you. For now.
{saga.settlement}'s medicine was stolen. They know who took it.
A {military.name} supply truck uses this road every few days. {warlord.name} wants what's on it, and nobody left to report it missing.
Before {warlord.name} moves on the checkpoint, the soldiers need to lose their radio.
Their radio's dead. I can hear them yelling at each other from here. Good. Get some rest. We go for the checkpoint soon.
Their radio's dead. You should hear them, running around like chickens. I love this part. Get some sleep. We go soon.
And afterwards? What happens to the settlement?
They pay like everyone else, and they stay alive. That's a better deal than the soldiers were offering them.
That depends on how nicely they ask. Don't worry about it.
You can't take on the {enemy.name} alone. The {wildcard.name} have people and guns and no reason to help anyone. Talk to them, and get your own side supplied for the fight.
Everybody wants our help all of a sudden. Last month you'd have shot us for our boots. Why should we bleed for your fight?
Because when they're done with us, they'll come for you.
[Persuade] Because whoever wins will remember who helped.
Then stay out of the way.
Probably true. Fine. We'll watch the back roads. Anybody running from the fight runs into us.
That's a reason I can sell to my people. We're in. Don't make us regret it.
Whatever they've got stored away when it's over. All of it.
Before anyone goes in, somebody has to know how many guns are inside
runs the {enemy.name}'s forward post. With them gone and the radio down, the main group can't call for help.
Meet your people at the staging point
Russian: Встретьтесь со своими на исходной позиции

Original English: [[Nobody says much. Somebody checks the same magazine three times.|Somebody's praying under their breath.|It's cold enough to see your breath.]]
Break the defenders at the gate
Free the people in the cooler
[[Is it over?|In here! The cooler!|The door's chained!]]
[tired] Well. You got in. I had forty people eating every day in here. You know how many of them are going to make it through the winter now? Neither do I.
[laughs] Look at this. Look at what you did to my place. You know, I'd have made you my second. You don't hesitate. I always liked that about you.
Why did you do it? Any of it?

Because nobody else was going to. The Guard was leaving, the farmers were praying, and people were starving in the meantime. I did what had to be done. I'm not going to apologize for keeping my people fed.
Because it was easy. Everything fell apart and nobody stopped me. I kept waiting for someone to. Turns out it was you.
If {lost.he} wants to hear it, {lost.he} can come and hear it from me. I'm not sending it through the person who's about to decide whether I live.
Leave the county. Don't come back.
You're going back to the settlement. They'll decide what happens to you.
[laughs] Yeah. I'd have done the same.
Mercy. Huh. You'll regret it. People usually do.
{warlord.name} was let go and left the county.
A trial. In front of farmers. That's the most civilized thing anyone around here has done since summer.
{warlord.name} was taken to {saga.settlement} to stand trial.
So that's it. I kept telling myself I'd refuse the orders when it came to it. I never did. You never even had to think about it.
